# Incorporating the Trial Class

## Trial, trial again

So far we've been working with a vidigi model that only runs a single replication.

However, we saw in earlier sessions how important it is to run **multiple replications** in simulation.

So how can we make vidigi play nicely with the trial class?

## Recapping the Trial Class

::: {.codewindow .python}
d_simple_one_step_model_vidigi_trial.py
```{.python}
class Trial:
    def __init__(self, param):
        self.param = param
        self.list_of_simulation_replications = []
        self.trial_mean_q_time_nurse = pd.NA
        self.trial_sd_q_time_nurse = pd.NA
        self.trial_perc_90_q_time_nurse = pd.NA

    def run_trial(self):
        for replication_id in range(self.param.num_replications):
            model_replication = Model(self.param)
            model_replication.run_model()
            patient_df = model_replication.convert_entity_list_to_dataframe(
                model_replication.list_of_patients
            )
            model_replication.calculate_run_results(patient_df)
            self.list_of_simulation_replications.append(model_replication)

    def calculate_trial_results(self):
        self.replication_df = pd.DataFrame(
            replication.__dict__ for replication in self.list_of_simulation_replications
        )

        self.trial_mean_q_time_nurse = self.replication_df["mean_q_time_nurse"].mean()

        self.trial_sd_q_time_nurse = self.replication_df["mean_q_time_nurse"].std()

        self.trial_perc_90_q_time_nurse = self.replication_df[
            "mean_q_time_nurse"
        ].quantile(0.9)
```
:::

## Tracking Replications - Tweaking the Model Class

Vidigi works best if it knows what run a trial came from.

So first (if we haven't already - if you're following best practice, you'll have that!), we're going to go and tweak our `Model` class to store the run number and pass it to our EventLogger.

::: {.codewindow .python}
d_simple_one_step_model_vidigi_trial.py
```{.python code-line-style="dim:1,focus:2,dim:3,focus:4,dim:5-7,focus:8" code-line-style-preset="emphasis"}
class Model:
    def __init__(self, param, replication_id): # UPDATED
        self.param = param
        self.replication_id = replication_id  # NEW
        self.env = simpy.Environment()
        self.patient_counter = 0
        ...
        self.logger = EventLogger(env=self.env, run_number=self.replication_id) # UPDATED
```
:::

## Tracking Replications - Adding a new import

We're going to be making use of Vidigi's `TrialLogger` class. This takes multiple EventLogger objects and allows us to do fancy things with them!

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='40%'}
::: {style='font-size: 85%;'}
First, we update our import statement.
:::
:::

::: {.column width='60%'}
::: {style='font-size: 85%;'}
```{.python}
from vidigi.logging import EventLogger, TrialLogger # UPDATED
```
:::
:::

::::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='40%'}
::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
Next, we need to update our `__init__` method to set up an attribute to store this object in.

We initialise an empty TrialLogger so we can add our EventLogger objects to it as we go.
:::
:::

::: {.column width='60%'}
::: {.codewindow .python}
d_simple_one_step_model_vidigi_trial.py
```{.python code-line-style="focus:1-2,dim:3-7,focus:8" code-line-style-preset="emphasis"}
class Trial:
    def __init__(self, param):
        self.param = param
        self.list_of_simulation_replications = []
        self.trial_mean_q_time_nurse = pd.NA
        self.trial_sd_q_time_nurse = pd.NA
        self.trial_perc_90_q_time_nurse = pd.NA
        self.trial_logger = TrialLogger()  # NEW
```
:::
:::

::::

## Tracking Replications - Tweaking the Trial Class

We now just pass our replication_id into the model in the `run_trial()` method (again - this part might already have been done in your model).

We then add our log to the `trial_logger` in every round of the loop.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='80%'}
::: {.codewindow .python}
d_simple_one_step_model_vidigi_trial.py
```{.python code-line-style="focus:1-3,dim:4-9,focus:10" code-line-style-preset="emphasis"}
def run_trial(self):
    for replication_id in range(self.param.num_replications):
        model_replication = Model(self.param, replication_id) # UPDATED
        model_replication.run_model()
        patient_df = model_replication.convert_entity_list_to_dataframe(
            model_replication.list_of_patients
        )
        model_replication.calculate_run_results(patient_df)
        self.list_of_simulation_replications.append(model_replication)
        self.trial_logger.add_log(model_replication.logger) # NEW
```
:::

:::

::: {.column width='20%'}
::: {.value-box fragment="fade-in" icon="fa-solid fa-triangle-exclamation" icon-position="top" align="center" color="bg-amber" font-size=0.9rem}
Note that the replication_id will count from 0
:::
:::

::::


## Getting a run from the TrialLogger

Now we need to update our code to grab an event log for animation.

`TrialLogger` provides a useful helper method called `.get_log_by_run`.

We can pass in any run number, and also choose whether it should be returned as an `EventLogger` object, or as a dataframe.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='20%'}
**Before**
:::

::: {.column width='80%'}
::: {.codewindow .python}
c_simple_one_step_model_vidigi_resources.py
```{.python}
my_event_log = my_model.get_vidigi_event_log()
```
:::
:::

::::




:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='20%'}
**After**
:::

::: {.column width='80%'}
::: {.codewindow .python}
d_simple_one_step_model_vidigi_trial.py
```{.python}
my_event_log = my_trial.trial_logger.get_log_by_run(run=2, as_df=True)
```
:::

:::

::::


::: {.value-box icon="fa-solid fa-lightbulb" icon-position="left" align="center" color="bg-green"}
Now we can regenerate the animation for different runs by just changing what we pass to that `run` parameter!
:::

```{python}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| label: initiate-trial-example
from sample_code.d_simple_one_step_model_vidigi_trial import Param, Trial

my_params = Param(mean_patient_inter=3, num_nurses=2, mean_nurse_consult_time=10, num_replications=10)
my_trial = Trial(my_params)
my_trial.run_trial()
my_trial.calculate_trial_results()

import plotly.io as pio
pio.renderers.default = "notebook"
```
